newsitem.title: USA: Nasdaq composite dragged down by Microsoft, Intel.
newsitem.headline: Nasdaq composite dragged down by Microsoft, Intel.

text.p: Nasdaq stocks finished down on Thursday, dragged off an early rise by profit-taking in Microsoft Corp and Intel Corp.
The Nasdaq composite index fell 6.86 points, or 0.54 percent, finishing unoffically at 1258.08, more than 10 points off the day's high of 1268.62 reached just after the market opened.
Declining issues outnumbered gainers 2253 to 1964. The session yielded 176 new highs and 126 new lows.
Unofficial trading volume was about 587 million shares.
"The Nasdaq is heavily weighted to the big guys like Microsoft and Intel and it fell off" on profit-taking, said Alfred Kugel, investment strategist at Stein Roe in Chicago.

"Those two are kind of the bellwether for technology stocks and it spilled over into other techs," he said, adding that the companies have seen steady rises since the U.S. Presidential election on Nov 4.
Microsoft fell 2-7/8 to 150-3/8 and Intel, which led the most active list, was off two to 118-7/8.
